newsitem.title: UK: HSBC's Knox to step down as director.
newsitem.headline: HSBC's Knox to step down as director.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc said on Tuesday that Northrup Knox would step down as a director from December 15 and would be retiring as chairman of HSBC Americas Inc and Marine Midland Bank at the end of the year.
Knox will be succeeded as chairman of HSBC Americas Inc. and Marine Midland Bank, by John Bond, group chief executive of HSBC Holdings, from January 1, 1997, the banking giant said.

Knox is the third generation of the Knox family to serve as chairman of Marine Midland Bank and its predecessors. His father, Seymour Knox, served from 1942 to 1970. His grandfather, also called Seymour Knox, served from 1913 to 1915.
Northrup Knox, 67, became a director of Marine Midland Bank in 1973 and chairman of the bank and its U.S. parent company, then known as Marine Midland Banks, in 1988.

"Mr. Knox has been instrumental in the development of Marine Midland Bank into one of New York State's major financial services organisations, and we intend to continue to call upon him to give us the benefit of his counsel," Sir William Purves, the chairman of HSBC Holdings.
